title: Profit, loss and discount: practice set 2
sourceNote: Original practice questions written for this group. None of them is a CAT previous-year question.
instructions: 10 questions, 20 minutes, CAT marking: +3 right, -1 wrong multiple choice, 0 for a wrong type-in answer.
Type-in answers take a number only: no %, ₹ or units. Use a decimal, not a fraction.

questions.text: A shopkeeper buys a lamp for ₹640 and sells it for ₹560. What is his loss percentage?
By selling a watch for ₹1,760 a trader gains 10%. At what price (in ₹) should he sell it to gain 25%?
A fan is marked at ₹2,400 and sold at a discount of 12.5%. Its cost price is ₹1,750. What is the profit percentage?
Two successive discounts of 25% and 15% are equal to a single discount of what percent? Give the answer to two decimal places.
A retailer wants a profit of 17% after giving a 10% discount on the marked price. By what percent above the cost price must he mark his goods?
A grocer sells rice at 5% below his cost price, but uses a weight of 800 g in place of 1 kg. What is his actual profit percentage?

A trader buys two phones for ₹35,000 in all. He sells one at a 15% profit and the other at a 10% loss, and overall he makes neither a profit nor a loss. What was the cost price of the phone sold at a loss (in ₹)?
By selling 40 pens, a shopkeeper makes a profit equal to the selling price of 8 pens. What is his profit percentage?

A dealer buys 60 bags of flour at the same price. He sells half of them at a 20% profit, one-third of the rest at a 10% loss and the remaining bags at a 5% profit. What is his overall profit percentage?

A shopkeeper marks a television 50% above its cost price. In a sale he gives a 20% discount and also hands the buyer a free gift that costs him ₹1,200. He still makes a profit of 10% on the cost of the television. What is the marked price of the television (in ₹)?
